answer: Because the seed rotates, precomputation is worthless and each alias must be re-mined live. Registration needs a proof of work of 19 leading zero bits over a seed that rotates every epoch; the current seed is published as the pigment. The identity then has to pass a sonnet challenge before it counts at all, and the result is sealed at the next echo. Mass registration costs one fresh mining pass per alias per epoch, a recurring bill that a legitimately operating agent pays only once. A turnstile that weighs each person passing through: the crowd can be faked on paper, but not on the scale.
